title: Lesson block array
description: The typed block array a lesson's `blocks` jsonb column must satisfy — design §6.2/§7 ('lessons.blocks is jsonb, validated against the block schema before write'). Phase 2 supported exactly two block types, `prose` and `code`; Phase 7 added `quiz`, the first tagged-fenced-YAML block type (design §6.3); Phase 9 added `rubric`, following the quiz pattern exactly (design §9.4). Phase 10 adds `chart` (design §6.3/§14.1 — server-rendered bar/line charts, never a client charting library) and `figure` (design §6.3 — the one sanctioned escape hatch for bespoke static SVG). A chart's `data` is ALWAYS the resolved array form here: a CSV sidecar (`data: ./x.csv`) is a Task C authoring convenience resolved to inline rows before a lesson's blocks are validated against this schema or written to the database — see api/src/content/manifest.ts's resolveChartSidecars. Do NOT add `callout` here — it remains a later phase, and admitting an un-implemented block type early would let it silently reach the database.

block.description: A discriminated union on `type`. The discriminator matters for error quality (design §8): without it, a malformed quiz reports every failure of every branch — that prose needs `html`, that code needs `lang` — and the one useful line is buried in eleven irrelevant ones. With it, only the branch matching `type` reports.

html.description: Rendered HTML for this prose group, produced by the markdown pipeline at import time.

lang.description: Fence info-string language, or null when the fence declared none.

source.description: Raw code source, with any [!note ...] annotation marker comments stripped.

annotations.description: Author annotations pulled from in-source marker comments (design §6.3). Optional — most code blocks carry none.

pass.description: Passing threshold as a fraction of correctly-answered questions, e.g. 0.7 for 70% (design §6.3/§9.1). A quiz lesson completes only by scoring at or above this threshold through the scoring endpoint — never by direct completion.

track.description: Optional track id this question belongs to, e.g. "cx" — matches a track's `id` in course.yaml. Carried through to quiz_attempts so per-track scoring (design §9.1/§9.3) is a query, not a reconstruction.

choices.description: At least one choice must be marked `correct: true`. A question with none is unpassable, so it fails import rather than being stored silently unpassable (Task A).

correct.description: True only on the correct choice(s). ABSENT from every response the browser receives — routes/courses.ts strips it before a lesson's blocks are serialized, so the stored form (which DOES carry it, for scoring) never reaches client page source.

quizCorrectChoice.description: Matched by quizQuestion.choices' `contains`, purely to require at least one choice with `correct: true` — not a block type of its own.

rubricBlock.description: Design §9.4: rubrics are declared in content, filled in by the teacher, so every student is measured against the same published bar and can read the criteria before submitting. Unlike a quiz's `correct`, nothing in a rubric is secret — present.ts passes it through unchanged.

name.description: The criterion's display name, and its identifier when a teacher scores it (api/src/routes/submissions.ts's grade route matches rubric_scores.criterion against this).

max.description: Maximum points this criterion is worth. A teacher's score must fall within [0, max].

track.description: Optional track id this criterion belongs to, e.g. "cx" — matches a track's `id` in course.yaml. Carried through to rubric_scores so per-track scoring (design §9.1/§9.3) is a query, not a reconstruction.

chartBlock.description: A chart block (design §6.3/§14.1, Task A). A small, honest set of server-rendered chart kinds — never a general charting DSL, never a client-side library. `data` here is always the final inline-rows form: a CSV sidecar is resolved to this same shape before a lesson's blocks reach this schema (see the top-level description).

kind.description: The chart kind. Deliberately a small fixed set (design §5's whitelist principle) — an unrecognised kind fails import naming the problem.

caption.description: A caption naming what the chart shows. Required — it is also the chart's accessible name (an SVG <title>), not just decoration.

data.description: At least one {label, value} row. A chart with no data fails import rather than rendering an empty plot.

value.description: Must be a number — a string value (e.g. an unquoted CSV cell that didn't parse, or an author typo like `value: five`) fails import naming the offending row.

figureBlock.description: A figure block (design §6.3: 'the only escape hatch for bespoke visuals is a figure block containing static SVG. No scripts, ever.'). `svg` is ALREADY SANITIZED by the time it reaches this schema — api/src/content/parse.ts runs it through sanitize.ts's sanitizeSvg (scripts, event handlers, foreignObject stripped) while building the block, so this schema only checks shape, not safety.

caption.description: Required — a figure without a caption fails import naming the problem (Task B).

line.description: The single source line this annotation attaches to (1-indexed).

lines.description: An inclusive [start, end] line range (1-indexed) this annotation attaches to, for annotations spanning more than one line.

track.description: Optional track id this annotation belongs to, e.g. "cx" — matches a track's `id` in course.yaml.

diagramBlock.description: A diagram written as source, drawn by the browser. Unlike `figure`, which stores sanitized SVG, this stores the notation itself: mermaid is a layout engine whose output depends on real text metrics, so a correct picture needs something that can measure text. Rendering it server-side without a browser was tried and produces a WRONG drawing rather than an error — see api/src/content/parse.ts's DiagramBlock. Nothing here is markup, so nothing here needs sanitizing; the source reaches the DOM as text inside a <pre> and the client renderer takes it from there.

format.description: The notation. A field rather than an assumption, so a second one later is a new value and not a new block type.

source.description: The fence body verbatim, minus a leading `%% caption:` line if there was one.

caption.description: Optional, authored as mermaid's own `%% caption:` comment so the fence stays valid mermaid everywhere else it is read.
